The timetable checks out.
- CNBC reports the company plans to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19.
- The offering is 825 million shares at $70–$78.
- The European prospectus gives the same indicative dates, which remain subject to change.
- Pricing is not final until the final prospectus is filed.
- Demand looks strong. Bloomberg reported orders at about six times the shares available. The FT reported bankers expect to price above the range.
- Neither report is confirmed by the company. EDGAR showed no filing after Nov. 10, so the range is still $70–$78.

## 1. What to buy: AMZN (Amazon), about $266.66
This is the most direct large-cap, liquid way to own the IPO mark-up.
- **Largest stake:** Amazon will hold about 1.92 billion non-voting Class N shares after the offering, worth about $149.8B at $78.
- **More to come:** Another 1.56 billion shares, worth about $122B, will be issued later because of a 12% ownership cap.
- **Relative exposure:** Amazon's stake equals about 9% of its market value, against 4% for Alphabet.
- **It also sells compute to Anthropic:** Anthropic committed at least $110B to AWS through April 2036.
- **Not yet run up:** AMZN closed Nov 13 at $266.66. That is about 7.7% below its 52-week high.
- **Relatively resilient:** On Nov 12, Nvidia fell 7.6% while Amazon rose 2.3%. On Friday Amazon fell only 0.3%. That is a thin sample, though.

**Why not the others**
- **Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, TSMC (placement buyers):** Their placement checks are tiny relative to their size. At the midpoint, Google and Nvidia buy about $10B each, AMD $2.5B, and Broadcom, Micron and Microsoft about $1B each. The bigger issue is that Nvidia reports Nov 17, the day before pricing. Options imply a roughly 9% swing. That is a coin flip that has nothing to do with Anthropic.
- **Alphabet (GOOGL):** Its stake is similar in dollars, but it is only about 4% of its value. It also has its own overhang. Alphabet booked an $8.7B loss tied to the SpaceX drop in Q3, and shares fell more than 12% on Oct. 29 after an earnings miss.
- **Closed-end funds and ETFs (DXYZ, AGIX):** They hold Anthropic, but premiums on closed-end funds holding IPO candidates tend to collapse after the underlying lists. Their NAV premiums are not something I could verify today.
- **Space-stock precedent:** The SpaceX debut is a warning about proxies that don't own the stock. Rocket Lab, Redwire and Intuitive Machines each dropped at least 10% as SpaceX began trading.

## 2. When to buy
**Monday, Nov 16, about 10:00 AM ET, with a limit order.**
- I'd skip the opening auction. The Empire State survey is at 8:30 and Fed President Williams speaks at 9:05.
- AMZN was already indicated about 0.9% lower after hours Friday. I can't see weekend or Monday pre-market news, so check the price before buying.

## 3. When to sell
**Primary exit: Thursday, Nov 19, about 3:45 PM ET, on the first trading day.** Sell before the close rather than holding into Friday.
- **Why then:** Amazon's stake gets marked to a real ANT price that day. Holding past it adds "sell the news" and fund-rebalancing risk with no new catalyst.
- **Index funds:** Nasdaq's fast-entry rule would add ANT to the Nasdaq-100 around Dec 21. That means index funds would sell other holdings later. This falls outside our window but is a reason not to linger.
- **Early exit:** If AMZN hits my target before then (say Wednesday), take the profit.
- **Why not Wednesday:** The SpaceX precedent argues for selling before listing day. Space stocks gave back most of Thursday's rally as traders sold the news. I'd still hold into Thursday, but I'm less sure of it than of the entry. Those were non-owners, and the evidence on owners is mixed. One source says EchoStar surged 11% on debut. Another says it dropped 9%.
- **Hard limit:** Out by the Nov 23 close either way.

## 4. Expected move, stop-loss, and abandon conditions
- **Expected move:** About +1% to +2%, with a plausible range of roughly −4% to +4%.
- **How I got that:** A 20% ANT pop on Amazon's roughly $142B stake at $74 is about $28B. That is only about 1% of Amazon's roughly $2.88T market value. The stock's own daily noise is larger.
- **Target:** about $274 (+2.7%).
- **Stop-loss:** about $259 (−2.9%). Friday's intraday range alone was about 2.3%, so a tight stop can be hit by noise.
- **Abandon the trade if:**
  - The IPO is postponed, or it prices at or below $70.
  - Nvidia's Tuesday report crushes AI sentiment and AMZN gaps down more than 3% on Wednesday.
  - The 10-year yield spikes further. It was at 5.15%.
  - AMZN rises more than 4% before Wednesday on no news. Take that profit.

## 5. Biggest risks
- **Macro:** Nvidia just posted its sixth straight weekly decline after the CEO's resignation. A Fed hike in December is fully priced. Democratic midterm gains raised regulatory worries for AI. That backdrop can swamp any Anthropic effect.
- **Funding drain:** After SpaceX, VandaTrack said selling of AI winners may have funded retail purchases. Anthropic is raising far more than SpaceX did, so mega-cap AI names could be sold to fund it. This is my inference.
- **Small stake effect:** Anthropic is under 10% of Amazon's value, and a bad AWS quarter would matter more than a great Anthropic one.
- **Already priced in?** Partly.
  - The above-range pricing is already reported, so it is not a surprise.
  - Amazon has not run up, so the rumor-buying is not obviously done.
  - One data set cited by TradingKey shows average 60-trading-day returns of −6% for buying on a first day. I couldn't see its methodology.
  - Since 1980, IPOs priced above range gained 50% on day one on average. That helps ANT more than Amazon, which only gets a fraction of the pop.
- **Weak debut:** One investor warned the worst outcome for the AI bubble would be an underperforming Anthropic IPO. A flat or negative debut would likely hit Amazon too.
- **Stale data:** Prices are from the Nov 13 close. I could not verify anything after Friday.

I put the chance this trade is profitable at my Thursday sell at only about 52%. If you want a trade with better odds, there isn't one here. The honest alternative is to skip it.

## Bottom line: **buy Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN)** — but only as a **small, event-driven trade**, and exit *before* Anthropic’s final IPO pricing becomes public.

This is not a high-confidence “free money” setup. The Anthropic event is real and the linkage to Amazon is stronger than for any other liquid U.S.-listed stock, but much of the underlying value is already reflected in Amazon’s reported investment marks and in the public knowledge of the AWS relationship.

### Verification of the IPO premise

The core report checks out. Anthropic’s amended registration materials show an offering of **825 million Class A shares at $70–$78**, a Nasdaq application under **ANT**, and a simultaneous **$26 billion Class N private placement** to named strategic investors. The European offering timetable says final price/allocation is expected **on or about Wednesday, November 18, 2026**, and Nasdaq trading is expected **Thursday, November 19, 2026**—while explicitly noting the timetable is subject to change. ([ipo.anthropic.com](https://ipo.anthropic.com/documents/us/prospectus.pdf))

The deal is enormous: at the range midpoint, it implies roughly a $1 trillion-plus equity valuation, and the prospectus says Anthropic generated $33.2 billion of revenue in the first nine months of 2026 but also reported a $104.0 billion net loss, including major financing-related accounting effects. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026072484/anthropicpbc-sx1ax2.htm))

## 1. What to buy: **AMZN**

**Buy AMZN, not NVDA, GOOGL, AMD, or a broad AI ETF.**

### Why Amazon is the best listed proxy

1. **It has the clearest and largest disclosed direct economic stake.**  
   Amazon’s September 30 10-Q shows:
   - Anthropic non-voting preferred stock on Amazon’s balance sheet of approximately **$92.5 billion**;
   - Anthropic convertible notes with estimated fair value of approximately **$146.2 billion**;
   - 164 million Anthropic non-voting preferred shares held as of September 30.  
   The IPO is therefore a genuine liquidity and price-discovery event for a very large Amazon asset—not merely a supplier relationship. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000040/amzn-20260930.htm))

2. **Amazon has a powerful operating linkage through AWS.**  
   Anthropic has committed to spend at least **$110 billion with Amazon from May 2026 through April 2036**, regardless of actual usage, with a shortfall true-up mechanism; the commitment is non-cancelable except for Amazon’s uncured material breach. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026072484/anthropicpbc-sx1ax2.htm))

3. **Amazon has incremental financing optionality tied to an IPO.**  
   Amazon’s 10-Q says it has a facility of up to $20 billion for Anthropic, with $15 billion remaining after Amazon’s additional investment. After an IPO, future draws can be in Anthropic common stock, subject to ownership limits. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000040/amzn-20260930.htm))

4. **It avoids a major confounder that makes NVDA a poor IPO proxy this week.**  
   Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 results after the market closes on **Tuesday, November 17**, so any move in NVDA is likely to be dominated by earnings, guidance, and company-specific news rather than Anthropic pricing. ([investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Sets-Conference-Call-for-Third-Quarter-Financial-Results/default.aspx?trk=public_post_comment-text))

### Why not Alphabet?

Alphabet is the runner-up because Google is investing **$10 billion** in Anthropic Class N stock at the IPO price and has an ownership cap of 14.99%. But Amazon’s reported Anthropic asset exposure is much larger relative to its own market value, and AWS has the more direct long-dated contracted-spend benefit. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026072484/anthropicpbc-sx1ax2.htm))

## 2. When to buy

**Buy AMZN on Monday, November 16, 2026, at 9:40 a.m. ET.**

Use a **limit order no higher than $268.00**. If AMZN opens materially above that—especially above $270—**skip the trade**. A large opening gap would mean the modest pre-pricing upside is likely already consumed.

AMZN’s most recently quoted price in this research was **$266.66**. 

The rationale for buying Monday rather than waiting:
- The public will focus on demand, allocations, price-talk, and possible upward pressure on the range during the roadshow’s final phase.
- Amazon is the cleanest “ownership plus AWS demand” proxy for that attention.
- Waiting until Wednesday risks buying immediately before the catalyst is resolved.

## 3. When to sell

**Sell AMZN on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 9:55 a.m. ET.**

That is deliberately **before** the indicated 10:00 a.m. ET publication window for Anthropic’s final price and allocation results. The timetable calls for pricing results on or about November 18, but it can change; the important point is to exit before the binary pricing outcome. ([assets.ctfassets.net](https://assets.ctfassets.net/yd8ev1715agv/1kajTB4XUtpCpjmStdRkX1/b8fe22030de40e57b7719b4d68871762/bafin-prospectus.pdf))

I would **not** hold AMZN for ANT’s first trading day on Thursday, November 19. By then:
- the IPO price is known;
- Amazon’s investment value is already broadly observable;
- the initial ANT trading premium could be spectacular, but AMZN will probably capture only a small fraction of it;
- a weak ANT opening, reduced deal size, or merely a $70–$78 price would turn the story into “buy the rumor, sell the news.”

There is no honest way to identify the time of “most profit” in advance. The best risk-adjusted exit is before final pricing, not after it.

## 4. Expected move, stop, and abandonment rules

|---|---:|
| Research price | **$266.66** |
| Expected pre-pricing move | **+2% to +3%** |
| Base target | **$273.50** |

| Time exit | **Wednesday, Nov. 18, 9:55 a.m. ET** |

The target represents a modest pre-event repricing, not an attempt to value Amazon’s full Anthropic stake. On an approximately $2.9 trillion Amazon market capitalization, even a large change in the mark of the Anthropic holdings does not automatically create a huge AMZN move—particularly because Amazon has already marked those assets upward. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000040/amzn-20260930.htm))

**Abandon the trade entirely if any of these occur before entry:**
1. Anthropic postpones, withdraws, or materially revises the November 18–19 timetable.
